decision: COMPUTE VENDOR SELECTED - Microsoft Azure, EU region

what_this_authorises.compute: A short-lived Azure Linux VM to run megacmd + the transcription pipeline
what_this_authorises.why_it_breaks_rule_2: content-os/AGENTS.md Rule 2 forbids any paid vendor. Azure is a paid vendor. This is an EXPLICIT OPERATOR WAIVER, scoped to the compute box only.
what_this_authorises.scoped_to: Compute and bandwidth for the NHB+ transcription run. Nothing else.
not_waived: Anything that persists after this run
what_this_authorises.expected_net_cost: USD 0 - the ~USD 26 of compute and egress draws against Azure's USD 200 / 30-day signup credit.
what_this_authorises.the_vm_is_destroyed_after: The run completes, or the ceiling is hit, whichever comes first.

why_azure: The only option where a FREE TIER ALLOWANCE, not just the credit, does real work: 100 GB/month egress free for 12 months from EU regions, plus B-series VMs free for 12 months.
EU region (West Europe / North Europe) keeps the whole path intra-EU: MEGA EU storage -> VM -> api.eu.deepgram.com, so the user's course content never crosses an ocean.
A reversible USD 1 card authorisation, refunded. Far less hostile than Oracle's signup path, which already failed.

fallback_if_azure_card_fails.why: USD 5 signup credit covers 72 h on a 2 vCPU / 2 GiB droplet at USD 1.29, with 2,000 GiB included outbound - far above the ~640 GB this job needs. Lowest risk of a surprise bill.
fallback_if_azure_card_fails.note: DigitalOcean's famous USD 200 credit is DEAD - cut to USD 5 on 2026-07-15. Two independent research agents confirmed this.

deepgram_credit_status.reported_by_operator: sufficient credits held on the existing account
deepgram_credit_status.why: The account's API key is a SCOPED INFERENCE key. GET /v1/balances returns 404, and the project-scoped variants return 403 INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS requiring 'billing:read' or 'usage:read'. The balance is deliberately not visible to this key.
deepgram_credit_status.what_this_means_for_the_run: The USD 136.31 forecast is expected to draw on existing promotional credit rather than new spend. Forecast and actual remain recorded separately.
deepgram_credit_status.correction_to_prior_artifact: The 2026-10-14 Deepgram waiver recorded this as NEW spend. If the existing credit covers it, no new money is spent and the waiver's ceiling still governs the run.

constraints_carried_into_the_run: USD 136.31 is a CEILING for transcription, not a target.
Receipts written PER FILE as work proceeds. A crash between the last response and a batch summary discards every receipt earned, and the next run re-bills the corpus.
Run targets come from the manifest, never from a glob over the output directory - a glob that matches its own output re-charges everything, because the vendor bills per request.
The VM is destroyed when the run finishes. Nothing persists.
Deepgram's consent flag mip_opt_out=true is structural and sent on every request.
not_yet_probed: Whether Azure's card verification accepts the operator's card. The general rule that IS sourceable: Verve Classic is domestic-only and routinely rejected internationally; Verve Global usually works. Nigerian international spending caps run from roughly USD 100/month upward depending on bank. This is the most likely cause of the earlier Oracle signup failure and may affect Azure identically.
Whether the 100 GB/month free egress applies to the specific region chosen.
